uncited: *   **Input:** User interaction (mouse/keyboard) in the spatial domain (volume rendering viewport) and/or transfer function domain (widget).
*   **Output:** Real-time updates to the volume rendering (spatial domain) and the transfer function visualization (transfer function domain).
*   **Spatial Domain Widget:** Contains the volume rendering viewport.
*   **Transfer Function Widget:** Displays the transfer function.
This allows the user to see which spatial features correspond to the queried TF values.
A Gaussian falloff or a fixed radius in TF space is typical.
*   **Visualization Competition:** Displaying the entire 3D transfer function would compete visually with the main volume rendering.
*   **Unintuitive Changes:** Small changes to the transfer function may result in large unintuitive changes to the classified regions in the volume rendering.
The system must retrieve data values, compute derivatives, update the TF widget, and re-render the volume for every probe movement.
This requires efficient data access and rendering pipelines.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Standard volume rendering memory plus storage for the transfer function (LUT).
*   **When to Use:** When designing multi-dimensional transfer functions, exploring complex datasets, or when users need to understand the relationship between spatial features and their data values.
*   **When Not to Use:** When the feature is known to be poorly localized in TF space, or when the user prefers a traditional TF-first workflow.
It was developed to address the difficulty of specifying multi-dimensional transfer functions manually.
